item.title: Warriors' surprising turnaround has changed everything about their present - and future
item.description: Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry (30) smiles after the team's 126-119 overtime win over the Orlando Magic on Saturday in San Francisco. (Stephen Lam/S.F. Chronicle) The Golden State Warriors are heading out on their first extended road trip of the season and they're packing a few items that no one would have expected just two weeks ago. An 8-3 record. And a slot in the top four in the Western Conference. Yeah, it's early. Very early. The season is only 13% complete. There are many ups and downs, stories and challenges ahead. But after an 0-3 start that seemed to confirm the worst of the skeptics' scenarios, the Warriors have transformed into a team that has not only been fun to watch but is creating bright scenarios for the future. "We're doing all the things we need to convince ourselves we're the team we think we can be," Stephen Curry said recently. What is the cause of this dramatic change in fortunes and vibe? Is it the magic in the building, left over from the Valkyries' spectacular playoff run? Possibly, and I'm not even kidding. Synergy between teams and coworkers is a real thing. Winning teams raise the bar for all the other franchises in their market: sibling teams definitely push each other even more. The Warriors were totally invested in the Valkyries' success, showing up at games, repping their gear, celebrating with them. And the Valkyries reminded the veteran Warriors of all the joy that comes with winning together. Is it my provocative question to Curry on Warriors media day, when I asked him how it felt that some people don't expect them to even make the playoffs and he said "Damn!" and walked off the podium? I am kidding about that moment, specifically. But, in general, the Warriors are a very proud group and they were well aware of the lowered expectations surrounding a team that was once only spoken of in terms of championship runs. Starting 0-3 made that negative noise louder. "It's hard not to hear it," Curry said. "We try not to play into it. We hate losing." Is the turnaround the result of something that initially looked demoralizing but could end up being a blessing in disguise? The unavailability of Kristaps Porzingis ? Porzingis never even got his season started, has since stepped away from basketball and the Warriors stopped paying his salary. The development has meant that Steve Kerr has gone with a lineup that allows rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to play power forward instead of small forward, a better fit, and also to play Draymond Green at center where he continues to play well. Not waiting around for the theoretical return of Porzingis also means the Warriors know exactly where they stand when February's trade deadline rolls around. Or is this bounce in the Warriors' play due to just one factor? The new guy? "Yax," Curry has said, more than once, when asked what's different. item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Vikings’ Kirk Cousins’ last game with Minnesota came vs. Packers. What happened? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Minnesota Vikings will have Kirk Cousins back under center, setting up a reunion against a familiar rival. His first game back could come against the Green Bay Packers . Coincidentally, Green Bay also faced him in his final appearance with Minnesota in 2023. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that the Vikings acquired Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders before the trade deadline. Minnesota sent a 2027 third-round pick in exchange for the veteran quarterback. Cousins’ final game in purple ended with a painful injury despite his strong performance . He threw for 274 yards and two touchdowns in a Week 8 win over Green Bay. However, he tore his Achilles in the fourth quarter. Head coach Kevin O’Connell expressed the team’s heartbreak afterward. “Me personally, our whole team, our whole organization, we’re all hurting this morning for Kirk,” O’Connell said, per Grant Gordon of NFL.com. HEARTBREAKING: The last time Kirk Cousins played at Lambeau Field, he tore his Achilles, ending his 2023 season with the #Vikings . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) He was helped off the field unaware it would be his final game in Minnesota. 3 years later, he returns to the same stadium. pic.twitter.com/4ttVpvLt9o — MLFootball (@MLFootball) November 10, 2026 The injury ended Cousins’ 2023 season and his first chapter in Minnesota. He entered free agency the following offseason and signed a four-year, $180 million deal with the Atlanta Falcons. After two seasons in Atlanta, he joined the Raiders and delivered a strong 2026 campaign. Cousins could also reconnect with several familiar faces from his previous stint. That includes star wide receiver Justin Jefferson and tight end T.J. Hockenson, who were key targets during his time in Minnesota. He will also work again with O’Connell, who coached him during his final two seasons with the Vikings. Kirk Cousins completed 64.1% of his passes for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions in nine starts with Las Vegas. His return gives Minnesota an experienced quarterback as it pursues the NFC North title. Facing Green Bay again makes the comeback even more meaningful. item.title: Rams MUST explore signing Odell Beckham Jr
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams should waste little time exploring the possibility of bringing Odell Beckham Jr. back to Los Angeles. item.title: Yankees Reveal Whether Giancarlo Stanton Will Be Back With Team
item.description: New York Yankees designated hitter Giancarlo Stanton Giancarlo Stanton missed most of the New York Yankees' season this year, and there was speculation that the team could finally move on from him this winter. When healthy, Stanton is an impact bat with tons of power. However, he has not been healthy too often. He is 37 years old, and the Yankees owe him $15 million for next season. He has a $15 million club option with a $10 million buyout for 2028. Despite rumors of the Yankees potentially moving on, general manager Brian Cashman made it clear that Stanton is not going anywhere. "There's never been a time when he's healthy that he's not been impactful," Cashman said on Tuesday . "If he's healthy, I know he can impact. I know he can get streaky and all that stuff, but he's an impact hitter, and always has been. Hopefully we'll get a healthy Stanton. He's a big presence in our clubhouse, a great leader. He's wired right. He's doing everything he possibly can to impact us in a real positive way. He's not going anywhere. He'll be in spring training with us, without a doubt." Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! Stanton is 44 home runs shy of 500 and has a strong case for the Hall of Fame when he retires. He is strictly going to be a designated hitter, which means the Yankees will have to keep Aaron Judge in the outfield. Judge is a capable defender, but as he gets older, keeping him off his feet should become a priority. The Yankees saw what can happen to their offense when he's hurt, and moving him to a full-time designated hitter role soon should be considered. The Yankees cannot do that with Stanton on the team, so it looks like Judge will be in right field again next year. More MLB: Reds Slugger Wins 2026 NL Rookie Of The Year

So we ended up with a trade deadline that lacked much activity for this team.

item.title: Former Indiana quarterback Fernando Mendoza to start for Las Vegas Raiders
item.description: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 01: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders warms up prior to the game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on November 01, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s time at last. Fernando Mendoza, the former Indiana football quarterback, Heisman Trophy winner, Big Ten champion and national champion, will start at quarterback for the Las Vegas Raiders, per reporting from ESPN and NFL Network’s Ian Rapaport . The move comes after the Raiders traded starter Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings just before today’s NFL trade deadline. Mendoza, selected by Las Vegas with the first overall pick in this past spring’s NFL Draft, has sat behind Cousins for the first nine games of the season and now is set to lead the team for the remainder of the season. Mendoza made his NFL debut in relief of Cousins in the fourth quarter of a loss against the New England Patriots, completing six of his eight passing attempts for 48 yards. Trading Cousins says a few things about the Raiders’ thinking. For one, Las Vegas has lost five of its past six games after opening the season 3-0. The focus has clearly shifted from winning in 2026 to building for the future, and that means seeing what they have in Mendoza. For another, it says they’re comfortable sending Mendoza out there. He won’t have the easiest start. The Raiders return to action this Sunday at home against one of the top defenses in the NFL in the Seattle Seahawks. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Feyi-Waboso has scored nine tries in 17 appearances for England since making his Test debut against Italy in 2024. However, his progress with England has been checked by a string of injuries. He missed the 2025 Six Nations with a shoulder injury, while his 2026 tournament was ended by a hamstring injury sustained in training before England's opening-round win over Wales. He returned this summer, scoring in wins over Fiji and Argentina, but suffered an autumn-ending ankle injury in the first half of Sunday's match against Australia. Robinson, whose acceleration and side-step brought him 28 tries in 51 appearances for England between 2001 and 2007, tore his hamstring in the Rugby World Cup final defeat by South Africa in his final Test. "He is our Jason Robinson," said Sinfield, who played against Robinson during the pair's days in rugby league. "When you have a player who is that explosive and that powerful sometimes a run of injuries just happens. "He's across everything to do with his body and hopefully we get him back firing as soon as we can. "That collaboration [between England and Feyi-Waboso's club Exeter] is going be really important because these guys play a lot of rugby. "Making sure they're fit for those big games is going to be really important." England have the final say over the fitness and conditioning of centrally-contracted players such as Feyi-Waboso, but there have been disagreements in the past with Exeter over his treatment. Relations have since improved with England signing off Fey-Waboso's return for June's Prem final, only three weeks after he suffered a facial fracture. Feyi-Waboso played on after suffering his ankle injury in the 32nd minute of Sunday's 45-22 win over the Wallabies, hobbling his way to half-time before being replaced. Sinfield said that the desire of Feyi-Waboso, who is studying medicine, to stay on the pitch swayed the decision to keep him on. item.title: Fernando Mendoza gets 3-word message from Kirk Cousins after Raiders trade
item.description: Fernandomania has officially begun in the desert. With the Las Vegas Raiders trading quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings in before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, Las Vegas are expected to turn to Fernando Mendoza , the No. 1 pick in the draft earlier this year, under center. Mendoza is slated to make his first career start against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks at home on Sunday, Nov. 15 (4:05 ET). Mendoza’s lone regular-season action came during his debut, at the end of a Week 4 road loss to the New England Patriots on Oct. 11. He finished 6-for-8 passing for 48 yards. Mendoza’s first two opponents boast vaunted defensive units. Seattle’s defense, dubbed the “Dark Side” for a reason, did not allow a touchdown last week to the undermanned Arizona Cardinals. Looking ahead, the Raiders face the Denver Broncos on the road in Week 11. Denver ranks in the top 10 in points allowed per game (20.7), sacks (26) and takeaways (12). "I feel that Fernando has done a great job,” Cousins told reporters Oct. 26. “He has a bright future ahead. I'm going to try and go out there and play as well as I possibly can and try and win and give him a good example to learn from." On his Instagram story, Cousins offered a goodbye to “Raider Nation” and a message to Mendoza, whom Cousins tagged in the post. “Go get em (sic),” Cousins wrote. Toughening matters for Mendoza on the field will be the lack of a rushing attack for the Raiders. First-round talent Ashton Jeanty from the 2025 draft has not worked out, although rookie Mike Washington has shown some juice in the backfield. Still, Las Vegas ranks 31st in rushing yards per game (71.3) and is last in yards per rush (2.9). Similar to Cousins, Mendoza will likely have to shoulder much of the output in the Raiders’ offense. “The game has to be balanced,” head coach Klint Kubiak said following the team’s most recent loss to the San Francisco 49ers that dropped their record to 4-5. “You can’t be a running and throwing team when you're throwing it every time. That's not easy. “You got to start the game a lot faster. You got to go toe-to-toe in the first half so that the second half isn't a throwing fest.” The good news is that tight end Brock Bowers ranks ninth in the league in receiving yards and provides a crucial red-zone target with six touchdowns already this season. Wide receiver Tre Tucker emerged as a reliable downfield option for Cousins, which gives Mendoza more relief in the passing game. The 24-year-old appeared to finally turn a corner against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8, throwing for 304 yards and two touchdowns in Tennessee’s 43-36 overtime loss It was an encouraging performance for the former No. 1 overall pick, who finally delivered the kind of gutsy performance Titans fans have been waiting to see. However, head coach Robert Saleh chose to pump the brakes on Ward’s coming-out party. Saleh Isn’t Expecting Ward to Be Perfect for Titans Saleh offered a revealing assessment of Ward when speaking with reporters on Monday. “I would love to sit here and tell you it is going to keep on climbing with no hiccups, and he is going to have nine of the best games he’s ever had in his life,” Saleh said. “But we are going to continue working with him, continue finding ways to get better and we are going to ride the peaks and valleys and hopefully by the end of the year we’re hitting a stride where Cam is consistently playing at a high level.” Ward’s posted posting a 104.6 passer rating in Week 8. It was his first career 300-yard passing performance, and he managed to do it without rookie receiver Carnell Tate, one of Tennessee’s promising young offensive weapons. Ward also helped the Titans take the lead late in the fourth quarter, only for the defense to surrender the advantage before Cincinnati eventually won in overtime. Saleh was encouraged by what he saw, but he also pointed out that the quarterback wasn’t the only reason for the improved offensive performance. “The kid’s a fighter: he’s a really, really good football player, but it’s also an all-11 game from a protection standpoint, to a skill player making plays,” Saleh said after the Bengals game. item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers kicker Ben Sauls in a preseason game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Aug. 16, 2025. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now A former kicker of the Pittsburgh Steelers could soon have a new home in the NFL. The Miami Dolphins worked out former Pittsburgh Steelers kicker Ben Sauls on Tuesday, according to NFL insider Aaron Wilson of Houston’s KPRC2 . #Dolphins worked out Marcus Banks, Daniel Carlson, Cameron Dorner, Kahlef Hailassie, Chris Hilton, Austin Reed, Ben Sauls, Christopher Smith, Bailey Zappe — Aaron Wilson (@AaronWilson_NFL) November 10, 2026 Sauls, 25, was just released by the New York Giants in September and has been looking for his next opportunity since. Sauls played his collegiate career at the University of Pittsburgh and signed with the Steelers as an undrafted free agent out of the 2025 NFL Draft. He impressed during the preseason, making five of his six field goal attempts and going seven of seven on extra points. “Really happy for Ben Sauls. The work he was able to show us,” head coach Mike Tomlin said. “Good for him.” Pittsburgh Steelers kicker Ben Sauls during a preseason game against the Carolina Panthers on Aug. 21, 2025. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now However, Sauls’ future in Pittsburgh was always uncertain since the team already had two-time Pro Bowl kicker Chris Boswell on the roster. The Steelers did try to trade Sauls following his standout preseason performance, but they were unable to find a trade partner and waived him ahead of the cutdown day deadline. On Sept. 23, 2025, the Atlanta Falcons signed Sauls to their practice squad. He was then released on Nov. 4 and the Giants signed him one week later. Sauls’ time with the Steelers was brief, but he was still very appreciative of Pittsburgh’s veterans for showing him the ropes at the next level. “To have guys who have been there and done that for years. I mean, the age gap. I think the second youngest is 30, maybe 31. I just turned 24 a couple of weeks ago. I am a breath of fresh air for these guys. But they’ve been there, they’ve done that,” Sauls said. “They reassure me on the field. And to have them with me this whole way. That’s why we just got a silly picture of us. Because I really appreciate what they’ve done for me. And they really took me in and showed me the ropes.” In 2024, Sauls connected on 21 of 24 field goals and a perfect 44 of 44 on extra points at Pitt. He was selected to the Pro Football Focus All-American team and a Lou Groza Collegiate Place-Kicker Award Semifinalist. Overall, Sauls finished his college career hitting on 52 of 64 field-goal attempts, while averaging 63 yards per kickoff.
